critical_code_review_comments: Fix scope is minimal and correct: only /app/final frontend mantrasetu/MantraSetu-Saarthi-main/src/hooks/useSaarthiVoice.ts was touched. Dedicated 16kHz mic AudioContext + zero-gain sink + adaptive echo-tail hold + AUDIO_FRAME gating on !isPlayingRef are the right architectural fixes.

useSaarthiVoice.ts is very large (~3000+ lines). Consider splitting into: (a) audio capture module, (b) TTS playback module, (c) VAD/echo-tail module, (d) WS transport. Would greatly improve maintainability and future debuggability of audio-path bugs.

rca of the issue: Original bug: single 24kHz shared AudioContext piped TTS playback into the same graph as the mic capture; mic processor was also connected to audioCtx.destination, so Saarthi's own voice looped back through the simulated loudspeaker into the mic and was streamed to STT (52 frames, 4 echo buffers, MIC dead). Fix: (1) dedicated 16kHz micAudioCtx separate from the 24kHz TTS ctx, eliminating in-graph coupling and the 24->16 decimation; (2) terminate the mic processor chain in a zero-gain node instead of destination, so no capture-side audible loopback; (3) gate AUDIO_FRAME emission on !isPlayingRef + listening state, so the pre-roll ring doesn't drain while Saarthi is talking; (4) adaptive echo-tail hold that keeps the mic gated until measured input decays back to the room noise floor (hard-capped at 1500ms), superseding the earlier fixed 600/700ms window that still leaked reverb tail. Verified: fixed=0 echo buffers, 1 clean user buffer (user_band 0.116 vs saarthi_band 0.000016), MIC_ALIVE=true, 16kHz log present, echo-tail released to floor (not hard cap), 450ms cooldown preserved.
